title: Evaluating LLM Creativity through Long-Tail Performance
abstract: arXiv:2610.12998v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Creativity benchmarks for large language models (LLMs) vary widely in task and metric design. This raises the question of whether they capture a common notion of creativity. We propose that this shared target can be formalized as task-specific performance in the long tail of a reference input-output distribution, which describes how common input-output pairs are relative to a chosen source of text. We ground this proposition in the novelty-quality product formulation and evaluate it empirically across 15 benchmarks and 26 open-weight models, using n-gram absence from the pretraining data as a novelty proxy. Our results show that creativity benchmarks lie further in the tail regions than standard benchmarks. Moreover, on both creativity and standard benchmarks, model rankings from higher-tail subsets of each benchmark align more closely with human creativity judgments in LM-Arena. Building on these findings, we introduce q@Tail($\alpha$),

translated_title: 通过长尾表现评估大语言模型的创造力
translated_abstract: 针对大语言模型（LLM）的创造力基准在任务与指标设计上差异巨大，这引发了一个问题：这些基准是否捕捉到了同一个创造力概念。我们提出，这一共同目标可以被形式化为在参考输入-输出分布长尾部分的任务特定表现，该分布描述了输入-输出对相对于所选文本来源的常见程度。我们将这一命题建立在“新颖性-质量乘积”公式的基础上，并在15个基准和26个开源权重模型上进行了实证评估，使用n-gram在预训练数据中的缺失作为新颖性的代理指标。我们的结果表明，创造力基准比标准基准更深入地处于长尾区域。此外，无论在创造力基准还是标准基准上，基于每个基准较高尾部子集得到的模型排名与LM-Arena中的人类创造力判断更加一致。基于这些发现，我们提出了q@Tail(α)指标。
tldr: 该论文提出将大语言模型的创造力形式化为参考输入-输出分布长尾部分的任务特定表现，并引入q@Tail(α)指标，实证发现基于较高尾部子集的模型排名与人类创造力判断更为一致。
en_tdlr: This paper formalizes LLM creativity as task-specific performance in the long tail of a reference input-output distribution, introduces the q@Tail(α) metric, and empirically shows that model rankings derived from higher-tail subsets align more closely with human creativity judgments.
